evidence.note: The counterplay the game wants exists and reads well: after Hall climbs, the menu offers 'Set up position / Pull off the top rope' at 84% and it lands — 'Hitman snaps off pull off the top rope — Hall takes 6 damage.'

But the CPU's climb-to-crossbody loop runs unpunished: 'Hall snaps off diving crossbody — Hitman takes 20 damage' at T8, T20, T34 and T50, plus a 20-damage springboard crossbody at T16. No loop-tax line ever fires against Hall's repeated climbs.
The player's answer to each knockdown is a forced single option — 'Fight to your feet' is the only listed choice on T9, T17, T19, T21, T29, T35 and T51, so seven turns contain no decision at all.

One real momentum swing late: 'Hitman snaps off straight right — Hall takes 7 damage. / Hall is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' followed by T43 and T45 offence pushing player momentum to 5 — but player HP is already 5, so it cannot become a comeback.
One-sided finish with no drama: Hitman goes 132 -> 1 while Hall only goes 132 -> 88, and the match ends on a clean 1-2-3 with near_fall_count 0.

Position context is clear: with Hall on TOP_ROPE the menu is all 'Set up position' options (pull_off_top 72%, hit_the_ropes, climb) plus recover, so the counter to a climb is discoverable from the prompt alone.
Being grappled reads correctly and honestly: state shows GRAPPLED for the player and the menu narrows to grapple_counter (51%) and break_grapple (61%), matching the documented escape options.

Confusing tax line: the player picks 'Climb down carefully' (intent 'Reset / recover', outcome 'hit') and the log reads 'Another empty climb — Hall takes the momentum.' The framing punishes the climb the player is abandoning, and 'hit' as an outcome for a momentum loss is misleading.

Advertised affordance does not appear: 'Hall is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' but the curated menu that turn is collar_elbow / climb / kick / punch / recover with no Big swing or Finish entry. Same at T41 when Hall is groggy again. Whether a power move was legal cannot be confirmed from the transcript (no valid_rules field), so this is a suspected curation gap rather than a proven hidden move.
single_choice_turns = 8 is felt: here the only option is break_grapple (61%), and on seven other turns the only option is get_up. The prompt is honest but stops functioning as a menu.
Damage readout misleads at the HP floor: 'Hitman takes 20 damage' while state HP goes from 2 to 1.

The chaotic policy surfaces states the aggressive seeds never reached — both wrestlers on TOP_ROPE at once (position_diversity 10 vs 6 in seeds 205/211), which opens a menu of top_rope_superplex 71% / hurricanrana 71% / top_rope_punch 77%.
Best moment of the match and a clear reason to try again: 'Hitman reverses the superplex — only 3 damage, and turns the tables!' from a top-rope-versus-top-rope standoff.
Against that, the middle of the match is a repeated beatdown — climb, diving crossbody for 20, get up, repeat — with the player never controlling the pace.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The varied positions and the top-rope superplex reversal at T48 are genuinely interesting, but being flattened 132-to-1 by the same diving crossbody four times is not a session to repeat as-is.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 223 with a policy that always answers a CPU climb with 'Pull off the top rope' (it hit for 6 at T13 and was offered again at T7 and T47) to measure whether the crossbody loop is actually counterable or whether the CPU climb needs its own loop tax.

evidence.note: Aerial spots hit hard and shift state: 'Hall snaps off diving crossbody — Hitman takes 20 damage' with position flipping to GROUNDED.
Top-rope reversal is the standout beat: 'Hitman reverses the superplex — only 3 damage, and turns the tables!' with momentum swinging from [5,3].
Groggy beats are well signposted across the match (T1, T36, T41) with 'is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' and clean recoveries like T37 'Hitman steadies themselves — they're back!'

Finish is flat compared with seed 205: the pinfall sequence is just 'Referee: 1… / 2… / 3! / *** PINFALL — Hall wins ***' (delays 1.0 and 1.5) with no finisher callback and no near-fall anywhere in the match.

top_issues.summary: A CPU-side loop persists with no loop tax at all: Hall climbs and lands a diving crossbody for 20 damage at T8, T20, T34 and T50. The anti-loop lines only ever fired once this match, and it was against the player's own dismount at T49 ('Another empty climb — Hall takes the momentum'). The tax appears not to apply to the CPU's repeated climb-to-dive pattern.
top_issues.suggested_area: loop tax coverage for CPU climb/aerial repetition

top_issues.summary: Eight single-choice turns, seven of them a forced 'Fight to your feet' after a knockdown (T9, T17, T19, T21, T29, T35, T51). After each 20-damage crossbody the player has no decision, which turns the beatdown into a spectator sequence.

T49 fires 'Another empty climb — Hall takes the momentum' on a move labelled 'Climb down carefully' with intent 'Reset / recover' and outcome 'hit'. Intent label, outcome field and log text disagree about what just happened.
top_issues.suggested_area: loop tax wording for dismount / outcome field

top_issues.summary: One-sided pacing: player HP 132 -> 1 versus CPU 132 -> 88 over 52 turns, zero near-falls, and turn_count fails the [8, 40] gate band.
